observations: Torah #121 of LM2 contains no bechina (parallel aspect / shared nature) declarations. The teaching is a pastoral encouragement for those who struggle with prayer, using practical advice (pray small portions with kavanna, think of gilgul as motivation) and analogies (the convert who rejoices at knowing words up to Baruch She'amar). The one occurrence of the root בחינ ('לפי בחינתו' — according to one's level) is idiomatic, not a structural identity statement. All conceptual relationships are eitza-type (cause-and-effect / practical advice): breaking prayer into portions LEADS TO ability to focus; considering gilgul LEADS TO motivation and self-encouragement. Since there are no bechina-connected concepts — not even a single bechina pair, let alone 3+ concepts forming an independent domain — no new packages can be proposed.
